Your active recurring business software totals **$210.83/month** across five services, alongside workspace and connectivity costs. Two specific tools stand out as primary candidates for review: **Amazon Web Services** and **Adobe Creative Cloud**.

[Display artifact omitted from public capture]

### High-priority tools to evaluate

1. **Audit Amazon Web Services ($82.44/mo)** — As a UX consultant using Webflow for hosting and prototyping, AWS is often running legacy client test instances, orphaned EBS volumes, or old dev environments. Checking your AWS Billing console by service line item can quickly pinpoint whether active compute is still required or if static prototypes can be archived.
2. **Review Adobe Creative Cloud ($59.99/mo) vs. Figma ($15.00/mo)** — If your day-to-day product design, wireframing, and client delivery happen in Figma, an all-apps Adobe suite may be underutilized. If you only need occasional asset editing, consider stepping down to a single-app plan or looking into one-time license alternatives.
3. **Consolidate Webflow ($39.00/mo) and client hosting** — If you maintain client demo sites or your portfolio on Webflow, ensure you aren't paying for overlapping staging on AWS or unused workspace seats.

### Core utility and workspace checks

- **Google Workspace ($14.40/mo)**: Lean and standard for business domain email, calendar, and client file storage.
- **WeWork Austin ($350.00/mo)**: Dedicated workspace is fully deductible on Schedule C, but worth calibrating against your actual monthly in-person desk utilization.
- **Spectrum Internet ($79.99/mo) & Visible Wireless ($35.00/mo)**: At $35/month, Visible is already very competitive; Spectrum can periodically be checked for promotional renewal pricing or speed-tier right-sizing.

Watch out: If you decide to adjust Adobe Creative Cloud, check your contract renewal date first. Adobe's standard annual plans billed monthly include an early termination fee of 50% of the remaining commitment if canceled mid-term, though negotiating via support chat or switching tiers can often bypass the charge.
